Headteacher’s Welcome
A strong mind needs a strong heart...
Welcome to Saint Christina’s. Nestled between Primrose Hill and Regent’s Park in the heart of St John’s Wood, we are a vibrant independent preparatory school for boys and girls aged 3-11.
Our identity as a co-educational Catholic school is shaped by an open and inclusive spirit, welcoming children of every background, belief, and story. Rooted in the true meaning of Catholic: universal, we celebrate the richness of our diversity, with kindness woven into the very fabric of our community. This is the golden thread that guides us - our compass, our core value, and the foundation of how we live, learn, and lead together.
Damien WalsheHeadteacher
Recent News
Stay up to date
My daughter is leaving Saint Christina’s academically prepared, but more importantly, imbued with the school values and knowing the importance of using these to drive the way she lives her life.
Saint Christina’s provided a nurturing and caring environment where our daughters thrived. From EYFS to KS2, the emphasis on pastoral care, arts, sport, and academics supported their all-round development. The strong parent community and wonderful playground make it a truly special place – especially for a school in Central London.
We feel incredibly lucky to have found such a gem. The staff go above and beyond to nurture every aspect of a child’s growth – academic, emotional, and social. Our son absolutely loves coming to school and has flourished in every way.
Choosing Saint Christina’s was the best decision we made. The children are taught values, stretched academically, and nurtured with exceptional care. Thanks to the school, they are confident, kind, and ready for their next adventures – with deep roots and lifelong friendships.
There’s nothing more reassuring than seeing your child skip into school every morning. Saint Christina’s is a place where children are stretched, supported, and part of a kind, aspirational community.
From day one, we felt supported and welcomed by the entire community. Our children are excited to go to school, and we’ve watched them flourish thanks to the warmth, dedication, and passion of the staff.
What makes Saint Christina’s truly special is the way every child’s wellbeing and happiness comes first. Our younger son arrived without English and is now thriving; our older son has grown in every way. The care and professionalism of the staff is exceptional – we are deeply grateful.
This school gets it right – a truly well-rounded education that nurtures curiosity, academic strength, and emotional wellbeing. The pastoral care is exceptional, and the community spirit lifts every family. We couldn’t ask for a better prep school.
Saint Christina’s is a beautiful school – not just in appearance, but in values. It nurtures children while grounding them in kindness, respect, and integrity. What more could you wish for your child?

Headteacher's Welcome
A strong mind needs a strong heart...
Saint Christina’s is an authentic and ambitious school community for boys and girls aged 3 to 11. Our children achieve excellent outcomes through an approach that is very much our own.
We are set in leafy St John’s Wood, between Regent’s Park and Primrose Hill, only moments from London Zoo and with excellent transport links.
We are ambitious for our children and we encourage them to think deeply, to question with confidence, and to act with integrity in all that they do. They are adventurous in their learning, take pride in their achievements and discover their own unique strengths.
What matters to us is that they leave not only inspired and challenged in their learning but also ready for the next step as thoughtful, grounded young people who know who they are and are comfortable in their own skin.
Academic lessons that stretch from English and Maths to Philosophy and STEM are complemented by a co-curricular programme rich in Music, Art, Drama and Sport. Children enjoy experiences that spark imagination and build resilience. They are given the space to try, to practise and to succeed. They develop the confidence to tackle new challenges with energy and joy.
Our Golden Thread of respect, diligence, inclusion and kindness runs through everything. It can be seen in the calm, purposeful atmosphere of our classrooms, in the supportive friendships that bind our children together and in how children give of themselves in service to others. We welcome children of every background, belief and story. Therefore, we are Catholic in the truest sense of the word: universal.
Words on a page will offer a glimpse of life at Saint Christina’s but the real story can only be felt when you visit. Step through our doors and you will see our values in action: in the ambition and joy of our children, in the dedication of our teachers, and in the strength of a community that truly knows how to draw the best out of each child.
“Leaders work in partnership with staff and pupils to create a harmonious and supportive school community.”
“It’s a truly exceptional place where children are loved, guided and inspired every single day."

Spiritual Life
Saint Christina’s is a Catholic school where prayer and worship guide us in caring for the world and each person in it. We begin by helping each child discover their God-given talents, ensuring that every individual feels valued, appreciated, and loved, regardless of faith or background.
The Sisters are at the heart of our community, bringing wisdom, innovation, and a deep commitment to the development of the school. Their forward-thinking approach and dedication to service continue to inspire our mission.
Faith is lived out through action, and Catholic children in Year 3 are prepared for the Sacraments of Reconciliation and First Communion, both of which take place in the convent chapel adjoining the school. Our commitment to Catholic Social Teaching is reflected in the charitable work and outreach initiatives that run throughout the year, encouraging all children to put their faith into practice.
Prayer and reflection are woven into daily life, from morning and end-of-day prayers to assemblies and whole-school Masses. Each Friday, a different class leads Mass, with parents warmly invited to join. Liturgies throughout the year mark key moments in the Christian calendar, deepening the children’s spiritual journey.
Our wider community is also welcome to attend Sunday Mass, celebrated at 10:00 a.m. in the chapel with the Handmaids of the Sacred Heart of Jesus.

pageCache.text:
Our Ethos and Aims
At Saint Christina’s we’re a part of God’s family, Where we live and learn and play in harmony. Everybody here strives to follow Christ’s way, In all that they think and do and say.
At Saint Christina’s we’re a part of God’s family, We respect diversity and individuality. We seek to excel in all that we do, Grow in God’s love and embrace Christ’s teaching, too!
At Saint Christina’s we pray and grow together, Treating everybody like a sister or a brother. We learn tolerance and co-operation, Embracing people from every nation.
‘We share and care and forgive for that is how Christ teaches us to live’
‘I come that they may have life and have it to the full’ John 10:10
In accordance with the Catholic ethos of our School, we aim:
At Saint Christina’s, we are a supportive, caring community where we prioritise looking out for one another and respecting our environment. Guided by our Golden Thread, we encourage qualities like resilience, perseverance, kindness, and respect, and these are the things we seek in our daily lives at school.
Our ethos shapes who we are and who we aim to be. We encourage children to think beyond themselves, consider those who are less fortunate, and engage with challenges that promote respect for every individual. Ultimately, we aim to create a safe, nurturing environment where children can express themselves, build confidence, and develop self-awareness, strength of character, and a sense of fairness in a world that often isn’t.
Saint Christina’s School was founded in 1949 by the Handmaids of the Sacred Heart of Jesus in the Ignatian tradition which places great value on learning in its purest sense, alongside the development of the skills of listening, reflection, self-knowledge and independence. The Handmaid’s believe that a child’s education should be a transformational experience, intellectually, emotionally and in terms of character, values and a sense of place in the world: the ‘pedagogy of the heart’.
At Saint Christina’s therefore you will find:
1. A school in which learning is highly prized.We take an ambitious approach to education, emphasising intellectual rigour, curiosity, creativity, and a passion for learning. Each child's progress is carefully monitored to ensure they reach their full potential. Our children consistently demonstrate a positive attitude to their learning and secure places in some of the most competitive secondary schools at 11+.
2. A school that places great importance on pastoral care.We are committed to ‘growing children’ in every sense, creating an environment where they feel safe, happy, and supported. Our Wellbeing Hub plays a central role, offering dedicated space for mental and physical wellbeing. Children are encouraged to openly express concerns and build confidence in their ability to cope with challenges. Support is provided through breakout groups, learning support, and emotional wellbeing sessions, including time with the ‘PAT’ dog for comfort and conversation. The strong, trusting relationships children have with their teachers, alongside these additional support structures, ensure every child thrives.
3. A school that places importance on the formation of character.We encourage the development of confidence, resilience, and compassion. Our goal is for children to leave Saint Christina’s as individuals who are kind, fair, and eager to contribute positively to any community. We encourage them to engage in thoughtful discussions, adapt ideas based on consideration, and make a meaningful difference in whatever path they choose.
Saint Christina’s School is dedicated to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children, and we expect our staff and volunteers to uphold this commitment. We aim to ensure that all children reach their full potential.

pageCache.text:
Science and STEM
Science and STEM learning at our school is all about curiosity, creativity and hands-on exploration. From investigating how our bodies work to exploring habitats, weather, light, forces and materials, our children experience a rich variety of exciting and meaningful topics throughout their time with us. Whether they’re growing plants in the garden, hunting for minibeasts on Primrose Hill, or testing the strength of different materials, every unit helps them understand the world around them.
We regularly enhance our science learning with virtual reality workshops, where children have explored outer space, the human body, and ways we can look after our planet. These immersive experiences help bring science to life in unforgettable ways.
Our passion for STEM extends beyond the classroom. We run three popular after-school STEM clubs for EYFS, KS1 and KS2, where children have the chance to engage in exciting experiments and use real-world equipment, including a 3D printer. Highlights include dissecting an eyeball in Year 6, designing and racing aerodynamic cars in the Formula 1 in Schools challenge, and taking part in team presentations to industry experts. Last year, our F1 challenge was combined with a STEM residential to Bristol, where children explored the Bristol Aerospace Museum, boarded the iconic Concorde, and visited the interactive science centre ‘We The Curious’.
From digging into soils and skeletons to solving science-themed mysteries in our light and electricity units, Science at our school inspires a love of discovery and prepares children to think like future scientists and engineers.

Saint Christina's children make excellent progress during their time within the School and gain places at an impressive range of senior schools.
We know that choosing a senior school can be a challenging process for families. Our expertise in the transfer to senior school means we work closely with parents to prepare the children for this move. The Head and his team have an extensive knowledge of secondary sector both within and beyond London and offer a personalised service that supports parents to find the best-fit school for their child to ensure they are happy, confident and motivated, with the necessary skills to succeed in their senior school, and beyond.
The process starts in Year 4 when our children start their journey towards 11+. Our aim is to have them ‘match fit’ by the end of Year 5 so they are ready to enter Year 6 fully focused on the 11+ process.
We work hard to ensure that our children aren’t just ready to sit the exams but are ready psychologically as well. When a child is happy at school, feeling confident and safe, there is nothing to restrict their emotional and intellectual growth. The knowledge of being good at what they do gives them confidence. The fact our children have been able to try so many different things during their time at Saint Christina’s means they have much to talk about in their senior school interviews.

Drama
All the children at Saint Christina’s enjoy a range of dramatic opportunities. This can happen during lessons, assemblies, workshops or on stage for one of our many Key Stage or class productions. This gives the children the chance to express themselves with confidence and encourages them to think and act creatively. It also helps to develop critical thinking and problem solving skills that can then be applied across all areas of learning. Drama develops emotional intelligence and helps children to understand the world around them.
Participating in one of our highly ambitious, professional and successful school productions encourages children to cooperate and work as part of a team. For those not wishing to take an acting or singing role, there are opportunities to help with lighting, costumes and scenery.
Productions have included Singin’ in the Rain, Mary Poppins, Annie, A Midsummer Night’s Dream, The Lion King, The Little Mermaid and, more recently, The Wizard of Oz.
LAMDA: Specialist Speech and Drama lessons
Speech and Drama lessons are available from Year 3 taught by our specialist acting tutor. These lessons, which are charged for separately, allow children to develop their dramatic and presentation skills in more detail, leading to LAMDA exams where appropriate. Children also have the opportunity to perform work from their Speech and Drama lessons to their parents in special assemblies.

Music
At Saint Christina’s music is an integral part of School life – children throughout the school, participate in a wide range of performances, musical activities and events, all of which have firmly established music as one of the strongest and most creative pillars of our school community.
The benefits that music brings to children are well reported and scientifically proven: accelerated brain development, refined listening skills, improved teamwork, communication and public speaking skills, increased resilience and a greater sense of overall wellbeing. Music lessons are also a great source of fun and joy, which cannot be overvalued in a healthy childhood.
Curriculum
EYFS lessons and those for Years 1 to 3 are based on an approach drawing on the pedagogical approaches of Kodaly and Dalcroze. This focuses on the whole body as a vehicle for music and musical expression, and helps to develop innate musicality in a unique way, with lessons often conducted barefoot and involving a wide range of movement in response to and as a key part of music-making. Singing is the primary focus, woven through a diverse curriculum which also includes instrumental playing, improvisation, reading notation and listening and responding to music.
In Years 4 to 6 there is an increased focus on growing musical skills. Topic work includes West African music, Brazilian samba, chair drumming, ukulele and a project on chords and how they are used in popular music. Children are given greater musical independence and the opportunity to work in groups on composition and performance projects. There is still a strong focus on singing, including more complex rounds, partner songs and music in two or three part harmony. In the summer term our annual school production involves all of Key Stage 2, so there is collaboration with the drama department to bring together what is always a wonderful show.
At Christmas, EYFS and Key Stage 1 have the opportunity to participate in a nativity play, bringing together songs, acting and movement. Children in Key Stage 2 take on the responsibility of leading our much-anticipated Carol Service, with each class bringing a song as well as the extra-curricular groups. All classes will also have the chance to lead a weekly Mass during the year.
EXTRA-CURRICULAR MUSIC AND CLUBS
We have a wide range of extra-curricular musical opportunities available – Key Stage 2 Choir, Little Voices (for Key Stage 1), Guitar Group, Orchestra, String Ensemble and Music Theory Club. The choirs perform regularly at school events, as well as in the local community where the opportunity arises. All the groups are popular and we are always looking to expand our offer based on children’s interests.
Children have the opportunity to take private instrumental or vocal tuition thanks to our talented team of peripatetic teachers, who provide lessons during the school day as well as some before school, after school and lunch time slots. Lessons are currently available on piano, guitar, ukulele, flute, violin, viola, cello, singing, trumpet and trombone.
There are termly music assemblies where children having lessons are encouraged to perform, and we also look to provide as many opportunities as possible for them to showcase their talent and develop their confidence.
Children are also able to make use of the school’s fantastic location through attending concerts and workshops given by renowned musicians that have included interactive performances by the London Symphony Orchestra, workshops by Gamelan music specialists at LSO St Luke’s and educational concerts presented by the London Philharmonic Orchestra. In recent times we have been very privileged to be able to attend rehearsals by the English Concert Orchestra in our very own Chapel.

pageCache.pageTitle: Communications With Parents - Saint Christina’s School
pageCache.text:
Communications With Parents
One of the reasons that Saint Christina’s is such a close knit, supportive and trusting community is because of the emphasis we place on regular, effective communication between the school and our parents.
Each week our parents receive the School Bulletin, which normally includes a letter from the Head or senior member of staff and gives a window into what has been happening in the school.
In addition to this, class teachers email parents each week with an update that includes news around learning and news of upcoming events. This means that all parents have the teacher’s email address in case they need it. Teachers will always meet with parents when needed and the Head runs an ‘open door’ policy.
Two parents’ evening take place each year and parents receive written reports at the end of each term. These may be organised as live or virtual events.
In the Early Years, we use the Early Excellence Tracker which can be accessed via most electronic devices enabling parents to monitor their child’s progress at any time and keep up to date with observations and comments.
Our website is regularly updated with information for current and prospective parents and we have an active presence on social media.

Parents' Link
Parents’ Link is a very important part of our school and we are very grateful for all their support. Founded over 20 years ago, Parents’ Link fosters a strong relationship between the parent body and school and builds on the family atmosphere that Saint Christina’s is well known for.
Through fundraising events and social gatherings, Parents’ Link is able to raise funds for School resources. Regular events in the calendar include a Summer Fair/BBQ, Quiz Night, Children's Pyjama & Popcorn Movie Nights and Children’s Discos – to mention just a few! All parents are automatically members and it is a great way to get involved in school life and meet other parents too. Everyone is welcome and there is no pressure to take on the running of any specific event, just turning up and giving a helping hand is greatly appreciated!

Thursday 13th February
As part of Children’s Mental Health Week, children in Ms Geary’s Art and Design Club explored growth in body, mind, and resilience through art. Inspired by Gustav Klimt’s Tree of Life, Reception, Year 1, and Year 2 children created their own interpretations using paint and collage.
Their artwork reflects the idea that, just like a tree, we grow by knowing ourselves, making good choices, and helping others flourish. Through creativity, we reinforce the importance of wellbeing, ensuring everyone feels welcome, valued, and supported in both mind and body.

Thursday 30th April
London Mini Marathon
We also want to celebrate a truly special event, the London Mini Marathon, which took place lastSaturday. This was an amazing day and a wonderful experience for everyone involved. Fifteen of ourchildren took part, supported by their parents. The children completed a warm-up led by Joe Wickesbefore embarking on the 1mile mile race which started at Horse Guards Parade and concluded at theMall. It was a very special experience and a memory I am sure they will remember for a very longtime. The event itself was incredibly inspiring, with children running alongside participants fromschools across London with over 20,000 children completing the course during the day. The sense ofpride, determination, and excitement was evident throughout the day, and every child should feelextremely proud of their accomplishment. The children all completed the race and received theirfinishing medals.

Art Design & Technology
Art encourages self-expression and creativity, builds confidence, and fosters a sense of individual identity, which is why we place such importance on it at Saint Christina’s for children of all age groups.
Art and Design & Technology (D&T) are taught by class teachers in some year groups, while a specialist teacher delivers lessons for others. We incorporate STEM activities into our curriculum and regularly arrange workshops to enhance children's artistic and design skills. Additionally, we organise day trips related to art to inspire and broaden the children’s creative experiences.
Children’s work is displayed throughout the school, and they have the opportunity to participate in art competitions.
Design and Technology lessons nurture creativity and innovation, allowing children to develop their designing and making skills. They work with a variety of materials, tools, and techniques and are encouraged to collaborate with their peers to find solutions to design problems. An essential aspect of D&T is fostering respect for the environment, as well as an awareness of health and safety for themselves and others.

Pastoral Care
At Saint Christina’s, the pastoral care of our children is at the heart of everything we do. We firmly believe that when children feel happy, secure, and safe, they can thrive. Our approach to pastoral care is fully integrated with our safeguarding practices, ensuring that every child is protected and supported in all areas of their school life.
While nurture is often linked to a tender or overly sympathetic approach, we’ve redefined it. We see nurture as an active, horticultural process, a bit like tending to a plant, where care, support, and guidance help children grow and become resilient. It’s not just about helping them pass exams; it's about preparing them for success in all areas of life.
We also recognise that some children may require additional support, and our approach includes tailored interventions for those with special educational needs, ensuring that each child receives the right level of care and attention.
Saint Christina’s is not a place of pressure but one where children can enjoy their childhood while being appropriately challenged. Our approach is to ‘draw out’ rather than ‘force out.’ Over their time with us, children take ownership of their learning, making significant progress and securing places at some of London’s most competitive secondary schools.
Each child at Saint Christina’s is valued for their individuality. We encourage them to work together, care for one another, and support their peers. Our assemblies, focusing on themes like friendship and anti-bullying, help children feel secure and valued, while ensuring they know who to turn to for help and support.

Extra Curricular
Saint Christina’s offers an impressive array of clubs and extra-curricular activities, catering to a diverse range of interest and talents. The clubs are held both before and after school, as well as during the lunch break. In line with our commitment to providing a forward-thinking education, we provide opportunities such as coding, F1 in Schools and STEM.
For children who are interested in sports, we offer a variety of clubs including netball, cricket and football, with judo being provided and led via a third-party instructor. In addition to this there are training sessions for children involved in teams, alongside a rich fixture list enabling the children to experience what it is like to compete against other schools.
In addition to this, children can explore their interest in the performing arts through various orchestras, ensembles, choirs, and performance groups. As they progress, they have the chance to pursue Music Theory alongside ABRSM instrumental examinations and LAMDA examinations. Ballet lessons are also available from EYFS to Year 4 through external providers.
For those who may be seeking cerebral stimulations, we offer clubs in Latin, reasoning, curiosity, and debate.
We also partner with another third-party provider to provide Sing ‘n’ Shake sessions, which are Music and Movement classes designed for pupil’s siblings, babies and toddlers, enhancing our commitment to providing a well-rounded educational and social experience for the children and the parents alike. If you are interested in participating you can apply through their website here: https://singnshake.com
There really is something for everyone!
